title: Scheduling & Notifications ⏰
description: Integrate cron‑ready design, email alerts, and command‑line options to control behaviour.

slides.title: Making It Cron‑Friendly 🕒
slides.content:
## Run Silently When Scheduled

We can check if the script is connected to a terminal (`-t 0`). If not, we suppress normal output and only log.

```bash
if [ -t 0 ]; then
  LOGFILE=""  # print to terminal
else
  LOGFILE="/var/log/cybron_guardian.log"
fi
```
Cron jobs aren't attached to a terminal, so this auto‑detection is useful.

slides.title: Cron‑Detection Snippet
slides.content: Set up logging based on whether the script runs interactively:
slides.codeSnippet:
if [ -t 0 ]; then
  echo "Running in terminal mode"
else
  LOGFILE="/var/log/cybron_guardian.log"
  exec > /dev/null 2>&1  # suppress stdout/stderr except log file
fi

quizData.question: What does `[ -t 0 ]` check?

options.text: If the script is run with bash

quizData.explanation: `-t fd` tests if file descriptor fd is opened on a terminal. fd 0 is stdin.

slides.title: Email Alert Function 📧
slides.content:
## Using `mail` or `sendmail`

A simple email function that uses the system's `mail` command (if available):
```bash
send_alert() {
  local subject="$1"
  local body="$2"
  echo "$body" | mail -s "$subject" "$ADMIN_EMAIL" 2>/dev/null || log ERROR "Failed to send email"
}
```
For systems without `mail`, you could fallback to writing to a specific alert file.

slides.title: send_alert Example
slides.content: Trigger an email on critical failure:
slides.codeSnippet: send_alert "Guardian Alert" "Backup of /data failed due to insufficient space."

quizData.question: The `mail` command is guaranteed to be installed on all Linux distributions.
quizData.explanation: It may need to be installed (e.g., `mailutils` or `mailx`). Always check availability or provide fallback.

slides.title: Adding Command‑Line Options 🎛️
slides.content:
## Make It Flexible

Use `getopts` to handle flags:
- `-c config` – specify config file.
- `-v` – verbose (force terminal mode).
- `-d` – dry‑run (show what would be done without executing).

This allows the same script to be used interactively and by cron.

slides.title: Option Parsing with getopts
Putting the Cron Entry Together 📅
slides.content:
## Example crontab

```
# Run Cybron Guardian every night at 2:30 AM
30 2 * * * /usr/local/bin/cybron_guardian.sh -c /etc/cybron.conf
```
The script will be silent, log to file, and send email only if something goes wrong.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content: Always include a `--help` message (or `-h`) that prints usage. It's the first thing a new user will try.
